title: Whip Practice
text: “I see. Kuro-chan seems to like slightly difficult speech patterns, so it’d be tiring if everyone talked the same way, huh?”
“That is indeed one of Kuro-chan’s strengths. If you wish, I shall leave it in her hands, I say.”
If Father wanted to entrust everything to Kuro-chan and have everyone turn out like Kuro-chan, then this Motoyasu would oblige.
“No, it’s fine. Thinking about the future, it’s better if it’s a Filolial that Motoyasu-kun wants to raise.”
“Understood, indeed.”

There should be no problem hatching Yuki-chan right away. Since Kuro-chan and the other Filolial-samas were already around, she would surely grow up happily. Yuki-chan, a slightly hot-tempered racing feather with strong leadership qualities, held plenty of promise for this loop, indeed.
“What about the other two?”
“This one is Kou, a lively Filolial-sama, indeed. Remarkably stable.”

Kou tended to grow into a similarly energetic Filolial-sama regardless of the loop. Unless raised with deliberate intention, there wasn’t much variation. Perhaps if raised with full attention from the very start, differences might emerge. Or perhaps if I didn’t take care of him and left it to Father or someone else instead. That possibility needed exploring too, indeed. Come to think of it, Father had once remarked that Kou resembled Filo-tan remarkably closely. Indeed… I couldn’t deny that Kou’s energetic nature bore some resemblance to Filo-tan’s. A gender-swapped Filo-tan, or rather… a boy version of Filo-tan, I say. But Father, that’s not quite right. All Filolial-samas carry a facet of Filo-tan within them, indeed.
“However, Kou does have a bit of a problem—he tends to look down on Father, and there are times when Father scolds him, leaving him trembling in fear, I say.”
“Scolded by me, huh… I don’t think I’m that scary though.”
Oh, but you are, indeed. Kou gets scolded for things like plotting to turn Mole into stew or eating Itsuki’s hair.
“Next is Sakura-chan. This child will become Filo-tan, indeed.”
“Ah, so this is the one who’ll become the Filo that Motoyasu-kun was looking for.”
“Indeed. But if raised normally, she’ll turn into Sakura-chan, so this time we’ll hold off on hatching her, keeping her in storage in order to follow the method learned in the previous loop, I say.”

Perhaps Kou and Sakura-chan should both be watched carefully for now. If Kou were raised at the wrong timing, he’d end up scolded by Father and grow timid. Since Big Sister’s friend was present this loop, there likely wouldn’t be an issue, but given how severely weakened Big Sister’s friend was, it remained a worry. Perhaps it would be better to wait until her stamina had mostly recovered. Big Sister herself would probably be fine too… but growing into the dignified Big Sister from the first world required going through all sorts of hardships, and since this loop had preemptively avoided those, it would likely be difficult. …In fact, it might be a good idea to contact Elephant early and entrust Kou to her care. I’d keep that in mind for now. And the most important matter was Sakura-chan. No, rather, Sakura-chan was Filo-tan. Since Father and the others had worked out the necessary steps to turn her into Filo-tan, hatching would have to wait until after that experiment, indeed.
“Right, got it. So we’re hatching Yuki-chan and Kou then?”

What should be done? Yuki-chan was decided, but Kou… should he be included in the experiment Father and the others devised for turning Sakura-chan into Filo-tan? When we deliberated on that back in the previous loop, it was an experiment abandoned due to ethical concerns—one only permissible because I was the one looping.

Specifically, the Clone Filolial-sama Plan. The whole point of experimenting through the loops was to avoid resorting to that. Come to think of it, Luna-chan was the key, indeed. Should Kou also be checked for a color change like Luna-chan? Luna-chan was an indigo Filolial-sama, but the first time she was hatched, she turned out white instead. If the same experiment were applied, Kou might also change color. And then there was Fleon-chan—Father and the others speculated that perhaps, without realizing it, I’d been giving her the same influence as Filo-tan. In the previous loop and the loop where I reunited with Fleon-chan, I’d given her the same type of feed both times. For the sake of the experiment, should Fleon-chan be raised on ordinary food this time to confirm the theory?

To begin with, Filolial-samas had core personality traits that varied between loops—some barely changing at all, others shifting dramatically. Kuro-chan and Black Thunder were clear examples of minimal change. Kuro-chan came across as a bit more childlike, but their manner of speech was quite similar.

Conversely, the fact that Filo-tan and Sakura-chan were the same Filolial-sama was something I failed to notice for the longest time, indeed. Energetic Filo-tan versus gentle, easygoing Sakura-chan. What’s more, Sakura-chan sometimes took on an adult form, making the variation even more drastic. Apparently, following Father and the others’ advice, it was possible to keep her in her younger form.

My thoughts were drifting, indeed. Conversely, what should be done to raise Kou into an adult form? Motoyasu, what kind of growth do you actually want for Kou? What I wanted for Kou was simply for him to grow up freely and without the trauma of being scolded and left trembling by Father. In other words… not that much change was needed at all!
“Indeed! Yuki-chan and Kou may both be hatched. However, Kou should later be entrusted to someone dependable, so he won’t end up looking down on Father, I say.”
“I see. Got it. Well, considering Kuro-chan’s appetite, if we raise too many Filolials it’ll be a hassle managing them on the slave trading side, so it’d help if you kept it moderate.”
“Understood, indeed!”
And so, having registered Yuki-chan and Kou, I activated the incubator.
“What was Father up to, I wonder?”
“I was getting some pointers from the monster merchant, then practicing swinging a whip a bit.”

Father had apparently been finalizing negotiations with the monster trader and picking up various tips along the way. Something about practicing whip-cracking too—it seemed he was behind the tent, whip in hand, practicing.
“Ow!? Hmm… it’s pretty tricky making sure it doesn’t count as a weapon.”

The weapon restriction seemed to be kicking in on Father, causing him to drop the whip several times. Alright, time for me to lend a hand, indeed. I’d bare my back and stand ready, literally shedding my clothes for the cause.
“Father, come on, I say!”
“Why is Motoyasu-kun stripping off his shirt and showing me his back while demanding that?”
“I too shall bare myself for the cause! Quite literally, I say!”
HAHAHA, indeed!
“Is Motoyasu-kun a masochist or something? Demanding to be whipped…”
“Practice makes perfect in all things, I say! Father!”
“I’m just practicing a little, that’s all…”

Come on, come on, indeed! After letting out a deep sigh, Father tried swinging the whip at me. Just as I’d expected, Father’s whip strike carried absolutely no pain whatsoever. Ah, how it brought back memories of our duel long ago. Back then, Father’s punches and kicks hadn’t hurt in the slightest either. Getting bitten by a balloon monster had honestly hurt more.
“The Spear Hero certainly seems remarkably sturdy…”
At that moment, the envoy from Siltvelt, who’d been watching this exchange between Father and me from near the tent, spoke up.
“It’s all thanks to Father, indeed. His gentle whip strikes feel like a refreshing morning breeze, gently coaxing one awake, I say.”
“That’s… quite the description. It’s making me feel strangely hollow.”
“And yet, deep in my heart, it strikes with a sharp, intense sensation. How about it? Care to try taking a hit yourself?”
“Why are you recommending this to him?”
“Since the Shield Hero apparently can’t attack, I must admit I’m rather curious. Would you mind granting me one strike as well?”
“No… being experimented on like this is making me feel pretty hollow too…”
Reluctantly, Father delivered a single whip strike to the Siltvelt envoy’s body.
“…I see. Indeed, this does feel remarkably like being stroked rather than struck.”
“Please don’t sound so convinced.”
“This definitely wouldn’t leave a wound—a gentle whip indeed. In that case, perhaps we’ll need some kind of pattern-based mechanism to simulate a reaction to the whip strike.”
“It’s purely for show, so it doesn’t need to go that far, you know?”
Apparently, this was strictly meant to be a demonstration whip-crack for use in circus performances.
“It would be best to add some sort of gimmick that leaves a red mark where the whip strikes.”
“Yeah, I’m already thinking along those lines.”
“What a troublesome business,” Father grumbled.
